Action Plan:
1. Suspected urinary tract infection with lower abdominal pain: Prescribed a 3-day course of antibiotics sent to the patient’s nominated pharmacy; to be taken twice daily for 3 days (specific antibiotic name/route/dose not documented).
2. Safety netting: Patient advised to contact the service urgently if pain worsens, if high temperature develops, if back pain appears, or if any new symptoms occur; and to recontact if not improving or if symptoms recur. Face-to-face assessment may be required if worsening or persistent.
3. Prescription logistics: Confirmed patient has an allocated pharmacy; prescription to be sent electronically.
4. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Chief complaint: Lower abdominal (midline/suprapubic) pain for 2 days.
- Associated symptoms: Feels hot/sweaty; measured temperature ~37.0°C; mild nausea; no vomiting. Slight increase in urinary frequency; reports increased thirst. Pink-tinged urine noted (possible hematuria). No dysuria. No back pain. No vaginal discharge. No upper abdominal pain or reflux. Bowel habit: constipation last week; now resolved; normal bowel movement 2 hours before consult; no blood in stool.
- Onset/duration: Acute, 2 days; no prior similar episodes.
- Travel: No recent travel.
- Gynecologic history: Regular periods; no intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding. Prior internal contraceptive implant, removed ~1 year ago.
- Past medical history: No significant conditions reported.
- Family history: Mother with breast cancer (treated early).
- Medications: No regular medications.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.
- Social: Lives with parents. Non-smoker. Alcohol ~1 beer, ~4 times/week.

Objective:
- Vitals (patient-reported): Temperature ~37.0°C.
- Physical exam: Not performed in this teleconsultation.
- Investigations: None performed (no urinalysis, urine culture, or pregnancy test documented).

Assessment & Plan:
1. Lower abdominal pain with urinary symptoms and hematuria:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis. Supported by DDx: “Acute uncomplicated cystitis” (High).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     • Ureterolithiasis or bladder stone (Medium per DDx): hematuria, suprapubic pain, frequency; less likely without flank/colicky pain.  
     • Early pregnancy-related issue, including ectopic (Low per DDx): reproductive age; no missed period/bleeding reported.  
     • Appendicitis (Low per DDx): lower abdominal pain and mild nausea; no RLQ localization/fever.  
     • Pelvic inflammatory disease (Low per DDx): absence of discharge/fever/dyspareunia.
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned: Antibiotic course prescribed for 3 days, to be taken twice daily (specific antibiotic name/route/dose not documented; allergy to amoxicillin noted). Safety net advice given: seek care if pain worsens, fever develops, back pain occurs, new symptoms arise, not improving, or recurrence; may require face-to-face assessment.
   - Relevant referrals: None documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  • No objective vitals except patient-reported temperature.  
  • No urinalysis or urine culture performed/documented.  
  • No pregnancy test documented.  
  • Pain severity/character not fully characterized; no abdominal exam.  
  • Sexual history details and last menstrual period not documented.  
  • Antibiotic name/route/dose not documented (only “twice daily for 3 days”).  
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Some audio/communication difficulties and brief incomplete responses; overall history obtainable but limited detail.
